episode_appearances.pitch: No-code web automation for consumer bookings and business workflows.
episode_appearances.offer: Mark Cuban offered $150,000 for 20%; Michael Rubin offered $150,000 for 15%; after the founders asked them to team up, Cuban and Rubin offered $300,000 for 30%. Maurice Bachelor and Joel Griffith accepted Cuban and Rubin’s joint $300,000 for 30% offer.

timeline.event: Bot-It aired in Season 15, Episode 3 and accepted Mark Cuban and Michael Rubin’s joint $300,000 for 30% offer.
A Trenton Journal profile described the Shark Tank result as a $300,000 'offer' and did not report that the transaction had closed.
Bot-it Inc. filed as a California foreign stock corporation, document 6179516, formed in Delaware; Maurice Bachelor was listed in principal roles.
Bot-It’s current site offered paid subscription tiers, business automation services and active signup flows.

registry_records.jurisdiction: California foreign registration / Delaware home jurisdiction
registry_records.status: active/good reported by California SOS-derived mirror; direct filing not captured
registry_records.limitation: A registry mirror reports the California foreign registration as active and attributes its data to the California Secretary of State. Direct BizFile entity detail was not retrievable here. The pre-Shark-Tank legal operator and any conversion into the 2024 corporation remain unresolved.

claims.text: Bot-It is operating as of 2026-09-09; its $300,000 on-air deal with Mark Cuban and Michael Rubin is not verified as closed.
Sony’s official clip and ABC’s roster independently fix the pitch at Season 15, Episode 3.

The public record supports an accepted on-air offer, but not a completed investment; later founder wording and absence from Cuban’s portfolio are consistent with a deal that did not close, but no primary termination document was found.

The current site is materially broader than ABC’s 2023 consumer-bot description, now marketing business, medical, accounting and workflow automation. This is a documented evolution in positioning, not evidence that any particular historical page was secretly edited.

episode_appearances.video_title: Bottle Breacher — ABC Beyond the Tank follow-up
episode_appearances.pitch: Personalized bottle openers made from decommissioned ammunition casings.
episode_appearances.offer: Kevin O’Leary offered $150,000 for 20%; Daymond John offered $200,000 for 25% contingent on licensing; Mark Cuban then joined O’Leary at $150,000 for 20%, split equally. Eli and Jen Crane accepted Mark Cuban and Kevin O’Leary’s $150,000 for 20% joint offer.

timeline.event: Bottle Breacher aired in Season 6, Episode 8; Eli and Jen Crane accepted Cuban and O’Leary’s $150,000 for 20% joint offer.
A Shark Tank update reported roughly 60,000 units sold after airing, website overload and rapid hiring/production expansion.
ABC promoted a Beyond the Tank segment in which Kevin O’Leary met with Bottle Breacher, strongly corroborating an ongoing post-show investor relationship.
Federal OSHA records show an inspection entry for Bottle Breacher LLC in Arizona.
Eli Crane’s federal House financial disclosure reports capital gains from Bottle Breacher LLC interests and purchase-loan receivables tied to sale of the entity to a buyer.
Bottle Breacher’s current company site identifies Mike as CEO and maintains an active operating team; the site continues to market Bottle Breacher products.

registry_records.status: current standing unresolved; federal and trademark records identify the LLC
registry_records.limitation: Direct Arizona entity detail was not captured in this environment. BBB reports incorporation on 2016-05-27; OSHA identifies Bottle Breacher LLC in 2021; active federal trademark records remain in Bottle Breacher, LLC’s name.

claims.text: Bottle Breacher is operating under post-founder ownership; the Cranes sold their interests in 2022 after a strongly corroborated Shark investment by Mark Cuban and Kevin O’Leary.

The 2022 founder exit is verified independently of current company narrative by Eli Crane’s House financial disclosure, which reports capital gains and a purchase loan from sale of Bottle Breacher LLC to a buyer.

Current ownership by Mike and Amber Wall is strongly corroborated by current company/team material and business profiles, but the underlying purchase agreement and exact percentage transferred were not retrieved.

Consumer-review platforms contain 2023-2025 allegations of delayed or unfulfilled orders and criticism of current ownership. These are customer allegations, not adjudicated findings, and they do not by themselves establish closure.

episode_appearances.pitch: An insulated stainless-steel holder that keeps glass beer bottles cold and protected.
episode_appearances.offer: Kevin O’Leary and Alex Rodriguez proposed a mixed equity/loan structure; Lori Greiner proposed $1 million for 3% plus a royalty; after negotiation, Mark Cuban and Lori Greiner jointly offered $1 million for 5% plus $1.50 per unit until $2 million was recouped. Adam Callinan and Matt Campbell accepted Mark Cuban and Lori Greiner’s $1 million for 5% plus $1.50-per-unit royalty until $2 million recoupment.

timeline.event: A federal consent judgment identified CamCal Enterprises, LLC d/b/a BottleKeeper as an Arizona LLC and owner of BottleKeeper patents in an infringement dispute.
BottleKeeper aired in Season 10, Episode 6 and accepted Cuban and Greiner’s $1 million/5% plus royalty offer.
Adam Callinan and Matthew Campbell assigned a BottleKeeper design patent application to CamCal Enterprises, LLC d/b/a BottleKeeper.
USPTO assignment history shows BottleKeeper intellectual property moving from CamCal Enterprises, LLC d/b/a BottleKeeper to BottleKeeper, LLC.
Canadian trademark records show a registered change in title from CamCal Enterprises, LLC to BottleKeeper, LLC, with a Houston, Texas address.
Founder Adam Callinan states BottleKeeper was acquired by Wind Point Partners/RTIC Outdoors in an eight-figure transaction.
The founders publicly describe the company as a completed exit; current RTIC offerings no longer clearly identify a standalone BottleKeeper line.

registry_records.status: state standing unresolved; 2021 federal/Canadian IP transfer verified
events: IP title transferred from CamCal Enterprises, LLC to BottleKeeper, LLC in 2021
registry_records.limitation: Primary federal and Canadian IP records establish CamCal as the Arizona operator and a 2021 transfer to BottleKeeper, LLC. State entity numbers/current standing for both entities were not directly captured.

claims.text: BottleKeeper was acquired in 2021 by Wind Point Partners/RTIC Outdoors; its Shark Tank deal with Mark Cuban and Lori Greiner did not close, and the standalone brand is no longer clearly marketed as an active product line.
Callinan directly states the Cuban/Greiner deal did not close; later secondary reporting describes roughly six months of diligence and a failed attempt at an alternate consulting arrangement.
The acquisition is supported by founder-authored/current professional biography material and independent business reporting; exact purchase price and acquisition agreement were not located.

The 2021 IP transfer from CamCal Enterprises to BottleKeeper, LLC is independently visible in public patent/trademark records and is consistent with a transaction process, but those records alone do not identify Wind Point/RTIC as the assignee.

Officially licensed Shark Tank Global metadata calls the clip season 10 episode 7, while contemporaneous broadcast-order sources identify the November 25, 2018 broadcast as season 10 episode 6; the tracker uses broadcast order and preserves the numbering conflict.

episode_appearances.video_title: Bounce Boot Camp — ABC official appearance index
episode_appearances.pitch: A mobile children’s fitness program built around inflatable obstacle courses.
episode_appearances.offer: No Shark made an investment offer; the Sharks questioned the scale, economics and Thomas Hill’s part-time commitment. All Sharks declined; Thomas Hill left without a deal.

timeline.event: A federal trademark application for BOUNCE BOOT CAMP was filed by Bounce Boot Camp LLC of Anthem, Arizona; the mark later registered as U.S. registration 4,181,010.
Bounce Boot Camp aired in Season 5, Episode 13; Hill asked $30,000 for 20% and received no deal.
Follow-up reporting described expansion through multiple operator/franchise locations after Shark Tank.

Bounce Boot Camp NY maintained an active service website with contact information, fitness programs, parties, scouts and team-building offerings; its About page credits Thomas Hill as founder of the concept.

registry_records.status: original LLC standing and current operator identity unresolved

registry_records.limitation: USPTO’s official gazette identifies BOUNCE BOOT CAMP LLC, Anthem, Arizona. Direct current Arizona entity standing and the legal/license relationship between that LLC, Thomas Hill and Bounce Boot Camp NY were not captured.

claims.text: The Bounce Boot Camp brand remains operating through at least an active New York operator, but the present legal standing of Thomas Hill’s original Arizona LLC and the license/franchise chain are unresolved.

Current operation is scoped to the brand/service network, not a claim that the original Arizona LLC remains active. The New York site is live, identifies the concept as founded by Thomas Hill, and advertises current services.
Later claims of multi-state/franchise growth are credible but the exact franchise agreements, operators and surviving locations were not independently reconstructed in this batch.
No evidence of bankruptcy, acquisition or a Shark transaction was located. Absence of those records in this bounded search is not proof none exist.
